sentences.text:
Heard learned Assistant Government Pleader Mr. Rahul Dave, Ms. Dharitri Pancholi and Ms.
Devanshi Patel for the appellants in the respective First Appeals and learned advocate Mr. A.V.
Prajapati for the respondents.
Perused the record.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:-
3.1. The land of the respondent-original claimants situated at Village Hathipura,
Taluka-Vijapur, District-Mehsana was acquired for construction of Dharoi Canal for the public purpose.
Notification under Section 4 of the Act was published on 07.03.2011.
Notification under Section 6 of the Act was published on 28.05.2012.

The award under Section 11 came to be passed on 26.06.2013, wherein the respondent original- claimants was awarded compensation @ Rs.60/- per square metres for the acquired lands by Special Land Acquisition Officer.

The said award was assailed before the learned Reference Court by the land owners under Section 18 of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2479/2020 ORDER DATED:
08/09/2025 undefined Act.

After considering the evidence on record, learned Reference Court partly allowed the references and awarded additional compensation of Rs.587.27 paise less Rs.60/-
per square metres for the acquired lands.
3.2. Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned enhancement of compensation, the State is before this Court by way of the captioned First Appeals.

4. Learned AGP contended that the compensation awarded by the Special Land Acquisition Officer is just and reasonable as award was passed after taking into consideration five years's sale instance of nearby areas.
Learned Reference Court has awarded higher amount of compensation by relying upon a award passed in LRC No.1 of 2014 of village Changod.

It is further submitted that claimants did not produce any evidence of three crops being taken in the year as alledged and has admitted that no account for income and expenses are maintained by claimants.

Claimants also did not produce any NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2479/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined evidence pertaining to potentiality of the land and therefore, the additional compensation which has been awarded is not just and proper.
Except above, no other submissions are canvassed by learned Assistant Government Pleader for the appellant-State.

5. Per contra, learned advocate for the claimants-respondent has supported impugned judgment and award and contended that learned Reference Court has considered the decision of village Changod which is a nearby village of the acquired lands.
Learned Reference Court has adopted a proper method and manner of granting additional compensation and in absence of contrary material, no intereference is required by this Court.

It is further submitted that the decision of village Changod was assailed before this Court by way of First Appeal Nos.309 of 2021 and allied matters and this Court has upheld the decision of village Changod passed in LAR Nos.1 to 7 of 2014.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2479/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined

sentences.text: I have considered the submissions made by learned advocates for the parties.
While deciding the reference cases, learned Reference Court has taken into consideration the judgment given in LAR Nos.1 to 7 of 2014 for the village Changod.

The evidence indicates that the acquired lands and the land of village Changod are very nearby villages and the learned Reference Court has adopted one of the approved methods of awarding compensation as contemplated under Section 23 of the Act.
Learned Reference Court awarded additional compensation of Rs.587.27 paise.
It further appears from the record that the purpose of acquisition of land of village Changod and the village Hathipura is the same.
The land in qeustion is an irrigated land.
It is well settled proposition of law that a comprable award can be passed as a basis for determining just and fair market price.
Learrned Reference Court has considered the decision of village Changod as a comparable evidence.

It also appears from the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2479/2020 ORDER DATED: 08/09/2025 undefined submissions of learned advocate for respondent that the decision passed in LRC No.1 of 2014 to 7 of 2014 has been upheld by Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in FA No.309 of 2021 and allied matters.
The said fact could not be controversted by learned AGP.
As no contrary material is pointed out by learned Assistant Government Pleader, I do not find any reason to interefere in the findings arrived at by learned Reference Court.
Resultantly, First Appeals fail and the same are dismissed.
7. The amount which has been deposited before the learned Reference Court be disbursed in favour of respective claimants after due identification and verification as per the prevailing procedure.
8. Record and Proceedings, if any, be sent back to the concerned Court / Tribunal forthwith.
